points.title: 童年启蒙
points.description: 1822年12月27日，路易·巴斯德出生于法国东部多尔的一个制革工人家庭。他的父亲让-约瑟夫·巴斯德是拿破仑军队退伍军人，后来成为一名制革匠。巴斯德在多尔度过了童年，展现出对绘画和自然的浓厚兴趣。这段早期生活培养了他细致观察的能力，为他后来的科学研究奠定了基础。1840年，他完成中学学业，展现出非凡的才华，特别是化学和绘画方面。
points.descriptionEn: Louis Pasteur was born on December 27, 1822, in Dole, France, to a tanning family. His father, Jean-Joseph Pasteur, was a former soldier in Napoleon's army who became a tanner. Pasteur spent his childhood in Dole, showing early interest in painting and nature. This period developed his keen observational skills that would later prove crucial in his scientific work. In 1840, he completed his secondary education, demonstrating exceptional talent, particularly in chemistry and art.

points.title: 求学巴黎
points.description: 1843年，巴斯德进入巴黎高等师范学院学习化学，师从著名化学家安托万·杰罗姆·巴拉尔。在这里，他开始了对酒石酸结晶的研究，这项研究后来成为他立体化学的奠基之作。1847年，巴斯德获得博士学位，并开始在巴黎任教。这一时期，他不仅掌握了扎实的化学知识，还培养了严谨的科学思维方法，为他后来的微生物学研究奠定了基础。
points.descriptionEn: In 1843, Pasteur entered the École Normale Supérieure in Paris to study chemistry under the renowned chemist Antoine Jérôme Balard. Here, he began his research on tartaric acid crystals, which later became the foundation of his work in stereochemistry. In 1847, Pasteur earned his doctorate and began teaching in Paris. During this period, he not only acquired solid chemical knowledge but also developed rigorous scientific thinking methods that would underpin his later microbiological research.

points.title: 发酵研究
points.description: 1854年，巴斯德被任命为里尔大学化学教授和科学系主任。在这里，他开始研究发酵现象，这是他科学生涯的重要转折点。当时普遍认为发酵是纯粹的化学过程，但巴斯德通过显微镜观察发现发酵是由微生物引起的。1857年，他发表《关于乳酸发酵的记录》，提出微生物理论，彻底改变了人们对发酵过程的理解。这一发现不仅解决了酿酒和丝绸工业的实际问题，也为他后来的微生物学研究奠定了基础。
points.descriptionEn: In 1854, Pasteur was appointed professor of chemistry and dean of the science faculty at the University of Lille. Here, he began his research on fermentation, a major turning point in his scientific career. It was commonly believed that fermentation was a purely chemical process, but Pasteur discovered through microscopic observation that fermentation was caused by microorganisms. In 1857, he published 'Mémoire sur la fermentation lactique,' proposing the germ theory of fermentation, which revolutionized understanding of the process. This discovery not only solved practical problems in brewing and silk industries but laid the foundation for his later microbiological research.

points.title: 微生物学奠基
points.description: 1867年，巴斯德回到巴黎，担任巴黎高等师范学院化学教授和实验室主任。这一时期，他完成了多项革命性研究：1865年，他证明了疾病是由微生物引起的，提出了细菌致病理论；1861年，他发明了巴氏消毒法，通过温和加热杀死液体中的有害微生物；1881年，他成功研制出炭疽疫苗；1885年，他开发出狂犬病疫苗，成功救治了一名被疯狗咬伤的男孩。这些成就使他成为现代微生物学的奠基人，彻底改变了医学和公共卫生领域。
points.descriptionEn: In 1867, Pasteur returned to Paris as professor of chemistry and laboratory director at the École Normale Supérieure. During this period, he completed several revolutionary studies: in 1865, he proved that diseases are caused by microorganisms, proposing the germ theory of disease; in 1861, he invented pasteurization, a process of mild heating to kill harmful microorganisms in liquids; in 1881, he successfully developed an anthrax vaccine; and in 1885, he created a rabies vaccine that successfully saved a boy bitten by a rabid dog. These achievements made him the founder of modern microbiology, revolutionizing medicine and public health.

points.title: 研究所创立
points.description: 1888年，在法国政府和其他国家的资助下，巴斯德在巴黎创立了巴斯德研究所，这是世界上第一个专门研究微生物的机构。他担任首任所长直至去世。研究所不仅进行科学研究，还生产疫苗和治疗传染病。巴斯德晚年虽然中风导致身体瘫痪，但仍然坚持工作，指导研究。1895年9月28日，巴斯德在巴黎逝世，享年72岁。他的研究所至今仍是世界领先的生物医学研究中心之一，继续着他的科学遗产。
points.descriptionEn: In 1888, with funding from the French government and other nations, Pasteur founded the Pasteur Institute in Paris, the world's first institution dedicated to microbiological research. He served as its first director until his death. The institute not only conducted scientific research but also produced vaccines and treated infectious diseases. In his later years, Pasteur suffered from paralysis due to a stroke but continued to work and direct research. On September 28, 1895, Pasteur died in Paris at the age of 72. His institute remains one of the world's leading biomedical research centers, continuing his scientific legacy.

supporter.zh: 巴斯德被誉为现代医学之父，他的微生物理论彻底改变了人类对疾病和发酵的理解。他的疫苗发明拯救了无数生命，巴氏消毒法至今仍在食品工业中广泛应用。巴斯德不仅是一位杰出的科学家，更是一位将科学应用于解决实际问题的典范，他的工作奠定了现代医学和微生物学的基础，对人类健康产生了不可估量的积极影响。
supporter.en: Pasteur is hailed as the father of modern medicine. His germ theory revolutionized human understanding of disease and fermentation. His vaccine inventions have saved countless lives, and pasteurization remains widely used in the food industry today. Pasteur was not only an exceptional scientist but also a model of applying science to solve practical problems. His work laid the foundation for modern medicine and microbiology, having immeasurably positive impacts on human health.

critic.zh: 尽管巴斯德的贡献巨大，但也存在一些争议。有批评者指出，巴斯德在实验中有时过于自信，甚至修改数据以支持自己的理论。此外，他的微生物理论虽然正确，但早期忽视了宿主免疫因素在疾病中的作用。巴斯德与同时代科学家罗伯特·科赫的竞争也引发了一些学术争议。他的狂犬病疫苗虽然成功，但缺乏现代临床试验的严格验证，这些方面反映了科学发展的历史局限性。
critic.en: Despite Pasteur's monumental contributions, some controversies exist. Critics note that Pasteur could be overly confident in his experiments and sometimes modified data to support his theories. Additionally, while his germ theory was correct, it initially overlooked the role of host immune factors in disease. His rivalry with contemporary scientist Robert Koch also sparked academic disputes. His rabies vaccine, though successful, lacked the rigorous validation of modern clinical trials, reflecting historical limitations in scientific development.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，巴斯德被定义为科学革命的象征人物，代表了19世纪科学实证主义的巅峰。他的名言'机会只偏爱有准备的头脑'成为科学精神的经典表达。巴斯德的形象超越了单纯的科学家，成为人类对抗疾病的象征。他的实验室、研究所和疫苗故事被广泛传播，成为科学进步的标志性案例。在流行文化中，巴斯德常被描绘为孤独的天才，与疾病斗争的英雄，这种形象虽有简化，但确实反映了他对人类健康的深远影响。
objective.en: In historical scholarship and popular culture, Pasteur is defined as a symbolic figure of the scientific revolution, representing the pinnacle of 19th-century scientific empiricism. His famous quote 'Chance favors only the prepared mind' has become a classic expression of scientific spirit. Pasteur's image transcends that of a mere scientist; he has become a symbol of humanity's fight against disease. His laboratory, institute, and vaccine stories are widely disseminated, serving as iconic examples of scientific progress. In popular culture, Pasteur is often depicted as a lonely genius and a hero fighting disease, a simplified image that nonetheless reflects his profound impact on human health.

self.zh: 机会只偏爱有准备的头脑。
self.en: Chance favors only the prepared mind.

others.zh: 巴斯德的发现比所有军队都更能保护人类。
others.en: Pasteur's discoveries have protected humanity more than all the armies.
